standard_prerequisites.use: Lets the resolution by finite free modules be built inductively.

standard_prerequisites.name: The cohomology-by-cohomology criterion for m-pseudo-coherence, and the passage from all degrees to pseudo-coherence
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Lemma \ref{lemma-cohomology-pseudo-coherent}, Lemma \ref{lemma-n-pseudo-module}, and Lemma \ref{lemma-pseudo-coherent}, cited at proof lines 16574-16579

core_obligations: Record the equivalence of coherence and finite presentation over a coherent ring (proof lines 16564-16565).
Show that a module which is a quotient of a finite free module with coherent kernel admits a resolution by finite free modules (proof lines 16566-16572).
Conclude the equivalence of the first two conditions using the cohomology criterion (proof lines 16573-16576).
Derive the final statement for all degrees (proof lines 16577-16579).
proof_roadmap: Resolution by finite free modules (proof lines 16566-16572).
Assembly via the cohomology criterion (proof lines 16573-16579).
difficulty_reason: The lemma characterises m-pseudo-coherence of a bounded above complex over a coherent ring by finiteness of the top cohomology in the bounding degree together with coherence, equivalently finite presentation, of the higher cohomology modules. The proof observes that over a coherent ring coherence and finite presentation agree, so two of the conditions coincide, and then shows that a module which is the quotient of a finite free module with coherent kernel has a resolution by finite free modules: the kernel is again coherent, so the procedure repeats, which is exactly the statement that the module is pseudo-coherent. The main equivalence is then assembled from the cohomology-by-cohomology criterion and the module-level statement, and the final sentence specialises to all degrees.
